text: Why does each method call get its own frame rather than sharing storage?
choices: So a method's locals cannot be disturbed by anything it calls, which is what makes recursion work and what makes a method's body private.
So the JIT can allocate registers independently for each method.
So exceptions can unwind to any frame without corrupting the ones above it.
So the garbage collector can reclaim locals as soon as a method returns.
explanation: The per-call frame is the mechanism behind Chapter 11's claim that a method's locals are not part of its interface. It is also what makes recursion coherent: `fact(5)` and `fact(4)` are simultaneously live with different values of `n`, which requires two storage locations. Chapter 25 builds the same thing by hand — a fresh `Env` per call, not per procedure — and the correspondence is exact.
